heroHeadline: BINUH Q1 2026: Security Forces Responsible for 69% of Casualties Including 69 Civilian Drone Deaths; PM Fils-Aimé Meets Pope Leo XIV at Vatican Amid Artibonite Crisis
heroSubtitle: The UN BINUH Q1 2026 report (released May 8, amplified internationally May 10, 2026) reveals that Haitian security forces were responsible for 69% of all Q1 2026 deaths and injuries — a counterintuitive figure driven primarily by HNP drone strikes that killed 69 civilians including 5 children, while gangs directly caused only 27% of documented casualties. This follows HRW's March 2026 report documenting 1,243 killed in 141 drone operations between March 2025 and January 2026, with Vectus Global (a US-licensed private military firm linked to Erik Prince) supporting the HNP Task Force with quadcopter-bomb technology in densely populated gang zones. Also emerging from the report: 292 sexual violence victims in Q1 (primarily girls aged 12–17) and the March 2026 execution of a 13-year-old for flying a kite — interpreted by gang members as a police signal. On the accountability front, 14 judges were appointed in March 2026 to newly established specialized courts for mass crimes and financial crimes. On the diplomatic front, PM Alix Didier Fils-Aimé received a papal audience with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on May 9 — discussions covered Haiti's socio-political situation, humanitarian emergency, migration (including the pending US Supreme Court TPS ruling for ~350,000 Haitian holders), and the role of the Catholic Church's 300 schools and 50 health facilities still operating in gang-affected Haiti. The PM returns to Port-au-Prince on May 11 as the Artibonite crisis deepens: IOM ETT-92 confirms 4,419 additional IDPs from May 2–7, Viv Ansanm destroyed the Marchand-Dessalines police station on May 7, and the ~545-person GSF advance force remains focused exclusively on Port-au-Prince, leaving Artibonite without international security support. Haiti's August 30 election remains in jeopardy: no electoral decree issued, voter registration not begun, 23 communes inaccessible.
